one_liner: PHP 7.1+ compiled to JVM bytecode; claims 2.5x over PHP 5.6 and 1.1x over 7.0, but is 13% slower than 7.4.
what_it_does: JPHP is an alternative PHP implementation that compiles PHP source to JVM bytecode, javac-style, and runs it on a Java 8+ VM. It covers most PHP 7.1-7.3 syntax and part of 7.4, and adds Java interop, threads, UTF-16 strings, and JavaFX/SWT GUI and HTTP-server extensions. It ships its own runtime library and package manager (jppm) instead of Zend's extensions, so it is a different platform rather than a php binary replacement.
how_it_is_fast: jphp-core walks the PHP AST and emits JVM bytecode with ASM 7.3. Values are boxed Memory objects (LongMemory, DoubleMemory, StringMemory, ReferenceMemory), but the compiler tracks INT, DOUBLE and constant stack items so arithmetic on known types skips boxing. Calls to built-ins marked immutable are constant-folded at compile time, and native functions are bound by direct INVOKESTATIC calls. The 'JIT' in the README is HotSpot's JIT working on that bytecode; JPHP has no JIT of its own.
when_to_use: Embedding PHP-syntax scripting in a Java/JVM application that needs to call Java classes directly.
Desktop or GUI tools written in PHP on JavaFX/SWT, which is what the DevelNext IDE was built on.
Legacy PHP 5.6-era CPU-bound scripts where a JVM deployment is acceptable and the claimed ~2.5x over PHP 5.6 matters.
Long-running JVM processes, such as its own HTTP server or multithreaded workers, where JIT warm-up is amortised.
when_not_to_use: Any deployment that can run PHP 7.4 or 8.x: by its own README JPHP is about 13% slower than PHP 7.4, and it was never compared with PHP 8's opcache JIT.
Code that depends on Zend extensions (curl, PCRE-specific runtime, mbstring and the like): the project says it does not plan to implement Zend's runtime libraries.
PHP 8 syntax or semantics: support stops at PHP 7.4 features, and some of those are partial (typed properties without references).

Production use needing fixes: no commits since 2020-07-07 and 40 open issues, including crashes (#414 ClassCastException, #403 and #396 parse crashes) and wrong arithmetic (#422 intdiv, #419 negative power).
Short CLI scripts, where JVM startup and warm-up outweigh any steady-state gain.

integration.form: module (Java jars org.develnext.jphp:jphp-* via Maven/Gradle, or jppm packages)
integration.dependencies: JVM; jphp-runtime, jphp-core (ASM 7.3.1); optional extensions (jphp-zend-ext for Zend-style functions, JSON, HTTP server, SQL, GUI)
integration.min_toolchain: Java 8 (sourceCompatibility 1.8); the build uses an old Gradle with `compile` configurations and Shadow plugin 4.0.3
integration.platforms: Any JVM platform (Linux, Windows, macOS); Android through the separate jphp-android project
integration.thread_safety: Ships php\lang\Thread and isolated Environment objects for multithreading; per-object thread-safety rules are not documented in what was read

gotchas: Harness asymmetry: StringBenchmark runs a different code path per engine, php\lib\Str methods on JPHP and strlen/strpos/strtoupper/str_replace on Zend, so the string part of the ratio does not compare like with like.

Harness design: 21 tiny micro-benchmarks (for example fib(1..5) per call, 8^4 empty loops) are each timed with microtime() around a single call, 10,000 times. Results are never used, so HotSpot is free to drop dead work. JVM warm-up is included. No per-benchmark times, JVM version, PHP build or opcache setting, or hardware are published.

UndefinedBenchmark reads an undefined constant, property and array key 8 times per run. On Zend PHP 7.2-7.4 the constant read raises E_WARNING, so with default CLI display settings Zend's time includes printing warnings; on PHP 8 it is a fatal Error. The error settings used are not documented.

The README's `./gradlew bench` command has no matching task in the root build.gradle, jppm.gradle, ext-template.gradle or the sandbox, packager and runtime build files; bench/ is a jppm package that settings.gradle does not include. Strings are UTF-16 Java strings, so byte-oriented string code can behave differently from Zend.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick JPHP over PHP JIT (php-src opcache JIT) or HHVM only when you need PHP syntax inside a JVM with direct Java interop. For raw speed, PHP 8 with the opcache JIT is maintained and faster than the PHP 7.4 that JPHP already trails.
verified_claims_summary: The only published result is a first-party README line: about 2.5x faster than PHP 5.6, about 1.1x faster than PHP 7.0 and about 13% slower than PHP 7.4 on the repo's own suite of 21 synthetic micro-benchmarks (bench/src). No JVM version, PHP build or opcache setting, hardware, or per-benchmark numbers are given.
status_note: Abandoned: last commit 2020-07-07, and a 2024 issue asking why it stalled has no maintainer reply. It is Apache-2.0 and usable for JVM-embedded PHP 7-style scripting, but it is only faster than obsolete Zend versions, and its benchmark has an asymmetric string test.
